retained_separation.argument: Use the already-stipulated endpoint norm bounds P_minus,P_plus in the source scalar-pair proof. Every threshold maximum is at most .999 Theta, by the listed exact comparisons, monotonicity of Theta, and two positive quadratics for the unbounded tails. For O-cross the positive .368/d term can be discarded. Thus scalar-pair uses at most .999 times the source separation cost. Retaining the remaining .001 of that cost in the unchanged matrix summation gives 2delta >= G+||gradientY||^2/1000+Omega_B/1000+C_sep/1000.
retained_separation.attribution: This retains margins in the stipulated source proof; it is not a new independent source theorem or an audit of the upstream certificates.

derivative_consequence.constant: M=sup_a q_second(a)/(q(a)-a)<infinity. q_second>0; the denominator is (log q) prime and positive.
derivative_consequence.finiteness: Smoothness handles compact intervals. At negative infinity q~phi, q_second=O(a^2 phi), q-a~|a|, so ratio tends0. At positive infinity q=a+a^(-1)+O(a^(-3)), q_second=2a^(-3)+O(a^(-5)), q-a~a^(-1), so ratio tends0. Differentiated Mills expansions were justified in earlier parent Fourier support.
derivative_consequence.spectral_estimate: For any real symmetric A and symmetric direction Z, Dq(A)[Z]-q_prime(A) Z has eigenbasis entry (q[ai,aj]-q_prime(ai))Zij. Since q_prime is M-Lipschitz as a function of log q, the coefficient has absolute value <=M|log q(ai)-log q(aj)|.
derivative_consequence.actual_transport: Apply to Z_r=partial_r A. Source r_ij>=1/16 gives sum_r E||partial_r J-q_prime(A)partial_r A||F^2 <=16M^2 C_sep. With partial_r A=X_r+partial_rY and ||q_prime(A)||op<=1, sum_r E||partial_rJ-q_prime(A)X_r||F^2 <=32M^2 C_sep+2||gradientY||^2 <=(64000M^2+4000)delta.
derivative_consequence.scope: All deficits and all dimensions, without ||B||op. The comparison tensor partial_rJ is fully symmetric because J is the actual Brenier Hessian. The matrices q_prime(A)X_r need not themselves be symmetric; their distance to that symmetric tensor is controlled.
derivative_consequence.limits: This uses retained actual transport separation, not a generic derivative bound for arbitrary A=L+Y. It does not yet convert to the required mixed-block energy or full exponential-factor recovery.
